newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares end firmer on dollar, economy.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares end firmer on dollar, economy.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed higher on Monday after two days of downward correction, partly because of the dollar's rally, traders and analysts said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 7,269.94 points, up 107.54 points or 1.50 percent.
"The rise across the board was partly due to the very strong dollar," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
"It was also due to purchases of mainly domestic investors as they thought the downward correction was over and it was worth starting to buy again," she said.
At midday the forint stood at 191.80/85 to the dollar, compared to 190.75/80 at opening. The strong dollar makes the forint, and thus Hungarian shares, cheaper for foreigners.
But an analyst said the market also reflected a generally positive assessment of the Hungarian economy and the earnings potential of companies.
"The general view is that it is a very well supported market," said Stephen O'Sullivan, head of eastern European research at MC-BBL Securities in London.

"It's partly due to the change in the crawling peg (for currency depreciation), but also the general feeling that the economy is doing quite well and corporate earnings should be strong," he said. "That's really what people are thinking about at the moment."
The Hungarian government's step to reduce the monthly crawling peg devaluation to one percent from 1.1 percent from August 15 was well received by analysts.

However, while most Budapest shares are traded by foreigners holding dollars, O'Sullivan added that in evaluating export-oriented companies one had to take into consideration forint movements not only against the dollar but also against other currencies, such as the German mark and the French franc.
"A weak forint helps exporters to get more out of the country but...the question is how much do you sell to dollar-denominated countries," he said.

In the first five months Hungary exported $7.042 billion and imported $8.079 billion, with Hungary's largest trade partner, Germany, accounting for $2.557 billion and $2.156 billion, respectively, according to data released last week by the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism.
Meanwhile, exports to the sixth largest trading partner, the United States, amounted to $251.2 million and the imports to $317.7 million.
On Monday's market, chemicals performed strongly, with TVK gaining 145 forints to 3,810 forints and BorsodChem 150 forints to 7,550.
OTP Bank closed at a new record high of 6,045 forints, up 220, meanwhile Inter-Europa Bank lost 1,000 forints to end at 48,000.
Curtainmaker Gardenia gained 200 forints to finish at 1,700, while mineral-water bottler and distributor Kekkuti firmed 60 forints to 1,500.
